words.tr: v. 限制；
words.ex: The school will curtail recess time during exams.
words.ex_cn: 学校在考试期间将缩短课间休息时间。
words.en: If you curtail something, you reduce or limit it.

words.tr: phrase. 减少污染水平；限制污染物排放
words.ex: The city plans to curtail pollution levels by banning old cars.
words.ex_cn: 该市计划通过禁止老旧汽车来减少污染水平。
words.en: To reduce the levels of pollution, typically through measures or actions aimed at decreasing harmful emissions or waste.

words.tr: v. 减少；削弱；减损；
words.ex: The noise will diminish after midnight.
words.ex_cn: 午夜后噪音会减少。
words.en: If something diminishes, or if something diminishes it, it becomes reduced in size, importance, or intensity.

words.tr: phrase. 减轻炎症；减少发炎
words.ex: The medicine helps to diminish inflammation in the joint.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物有助于减轻关节的炎症。
words.en: To reduce or lessen the severity of inflammation in the body.

words.tr: v. 减轻；缓解；
words.ex: Drugs can alleviate pain.
words.ex_cn: 药物可以减轻疼痛。
words.en: To make something less severe or intense.

words.tr: phrase. 减轻负担；缓解压力
words.ex: The new policy helps to alleviate the burden on poor families.
words.ex_cn: 新政策有助于减轻贫困家庭的负担。
words.en: To make a problem or burden less severe or easier to bear.

words.tr: v. 减轻；缓和；
words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.tr: phrase. 减轻影响；缓和作用
words.ex: Plant trees to mitigate the effect of pollution.
words.ex_cn: 种树以减轻污染的影响。
words.en: To mitigate the effect means to make something less severe, serious, or painful.

words.tr: adj. 简单的；
words.ex: The instructions were straightforward and easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很简单，容易遵循。
words.en: If you describe something as straightforward, you approve of it because it is easy to do or understand.

words.tr: phrase. 直截了当的解决方案；简单明了的解决办法
words.ex: The teacher gave a straightforward solution to the math problem.
words.ex_cn: 老师给出了一个简单的数学问题解决方案。
words.en: A straightforward solution is one that is simple and easy to understand, without any unnecessary complications.

words.tr: adj. 简单的；不复杂的；率真的
words.ex: The instructions are uncomplicated.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明很简单。
words.en: If you describe something as uncomplicated, you mean that it is simple and not difficult to understand or do.

words.tr: phrase. 不复杂的且易于遵循的；简单明了的
words.ex: The instructions are uncomplicated and easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这些说明简单易懂。
words.en: Simple and straightforward to understand or follow; not complicated.

words.tr: adj. 不需费力的；
words.ex: She made the dance look effortless.
words.ex_cn: 她让舞蹈看起来毫不费力。
words.en: If you describe something as effortless, you mean that it is done or achieved with very little difficulty or work, often as a result of great skill.

words.tr: v. 增强；
words.ex: She works out to augment her strength.
words.ex_cn: 她锻炼以增强力量。
words.en: If you augment something, you make it larger, stronger, or more effective by adding something to it.

words.tr: phrase. 提高国家生产力；增强国民生产效率
words.ex: The new machine will augment national productivity.
words.ex_cn: 这台新机器将提高国家生产力。
words.en: To increase or improve the productive output or efficiency of a nation's economy or workforce.

words.tr: v. 增强；提高；
words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.tr: phrase. 支持经济增长；加强经济扩张
words.ex: The government plans to bolster economic growth by lowering taxes.
words.ex_cn: 政府计划通过减税来促进经济增长。
words.en: To bolster economic growth means to support or strengthen the increase in the economic output of a country or region.

words.tr: v. 推动；
words.ex: The wind propels the sailboat forward.
words.ex_cn: 风推动帆船前进。
words.en: To propel something in a particular direction means to cause it to move in that direction.

words.tr: phrase. 推动可持续发展
words.ex: Renewable energy can propel sustainable development.
words.ex_cn: 可再生能源可以推动可持续发展。
words.en: To drive or push forward the development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs.

words.tr: v. 加速；加快；有助于
words.ex: He wants to expedite the process.
words.ex_cn: 他想加快这个过程。
words.en: To expedite something means to make it happen or be done more quickly.

words.tr: phrase. 显著加快进程；极大地促进某事的进行
words.ex: The new software will expedite the process significantly.
words.ex_cn: 新软件将显著加快这个过程。
words.en: To make a process or action happen much faster or more quickly.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.tr: phrase. 不可避免的趋势；必然趋势
words.ex: The rise of technology is an inevitable trend.
words.ex_cn: 科技的发展是一个不可避免的趋势。
words.en: An inevitable trend is a development or change that is certain to happen and cannot be avoided.

words.tr: adj. 全面的；综合的；
words.ex: The teacher gave a comprehensive review before the exam.
words.ex_cn: 老师在考试前给了一个全面的复习。
words.en: Something that is comprehensive includes everything that is needed or relevant.

words.tr: phrase. 全面的方法；综合性的处理方式
words.ex: The teacher uses a comprehensive approach to teach math.
words.ex_cn: 老师使用一种全面的方法来教数学。
words.en: A comprehensive approach refers to a method or strategy that covers all aspects or elements of a subject or problem, ensuring a thorough understanding or solution.

words.tr: adj. 到处存在的
words.ex: Smartphones are ubiquitous in modern life.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机在现代生活中无处不在。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as ubiquitous, you mean that they seem to be everywhere.

words.tr: phrase. 变得无处不在；变得普遍存在于各处
words.ex: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in daily life.
words.ex_cn: 智能手机在日常生活中变得无处不在。
words.en: To become present, or to seem to be present, everywhere at the same time.

words.tr: adj. 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；
words.ex: His answer was ambiguous and confused everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他的回答模棱两可，让所有人都感到困惑。
words.en: If you describe something as ambiguous, you mean that it is unclear or confusing because it can be understood in more than one way.

words.tr: phrase. 含义模糊的信息；不明确的信息；有歧义的信息
words.ex: The message gave ambiguous information.
words.ex_cn: 这条信息提供了模棱两可的信息。
words.en: Information that can be understood in more than one way; information that is not clear or is open to multiple interpretations.

words.tr: adj. 无可争辩的；
words.ex: The evidence is indisputable.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可争辩的。
words.en: Something that is indisputable is true and cannot be denied or questioned.

words.tr: phrase. 无可争议的事实；不容置疑的事实
words.ex: It is an indisputable fact that water boils at 100 degrees Celsius.
words.ex_cn: 水在100摄氏度沸腾是一个不可争议的事实。
words.en: A fact that is so obviously true that it cannot be argued against.

words.tr: adj. 不容置疑的；无可否认的
words.ex: The evidence is incontrovertible.
words.ex_cn: 证据是无可辩驳的。
words.en: If something is incontrovertible, it is definitely true and cannot be disputed.

words.tr: phrase. 无可辩驳的证据；确凿无疑的证据
words.ex: The video shows incontrovertible evidence of the crime.
words.ex_cn: 这段视频提供了无可辩驳的犯罪证据。
words.en: Evidence that is incontrovertible is impossible to dispute or argue against because it is so obviously true or certain.

words.tr: conj. 尽管；虽然；
words.ex: He passed the test, albeit with a low score.
words.ex_cn: 他通过了考试，尽管分数很低。
words.en: You use albeit to introduce a fact or comment which reduces the force or significance of what you have just said.

words.tr: phrase. 无中文释义
words.ex: He agreed to help, albeit reluctancy.
words.ex_cn: 他同意帮忙，尽管不情愿。
words.en: Although; even if.

words.tr: phrase. 同样地；同样道理；由于同样的原因
words.ex: He likes coffee; by the same token, he also likes tea.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢咖啡；同样地，他也喜欢茶。
words.en: used to mean that something you are about to say is also true, for the same reasons as what has just been said

words.tr: prep. 虽然；尽管；
words.ex: Notwithstanding the rain, they went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 虽然下着雨，他们还是去散步了。
words.en: In spite of; although.

words.tr: phrase. 总的来说；权衡之后；综合考虑
words.ex: On balance, he is happier now than before.
words.ex_cn: 总体来看，他现在比以前更快乐。
words.en: After considering all the facts, in general.

words.tr: adj. 过时的；废弃的；淘汰的；
words.ex: This phone is obsolete because it doesn't work with new apps.
words.ex_cn: 这部手机已经过时了，因为它不能使用新应用。
words.en: Something that is obsolete is no longer needed because something better has been invented.

words.tr: phrase. 有助于…的；有益于…的
words.ex_cn: 新鲜空气有益于健康。
words.en: To help bring about or make something possible.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.tr: phrase. 高收入的职业机会；有利可图的职业前景
words.ex: He found lucrative career opportunities in tech companies.
words.ex_cn: 他在科技公司找到了高薪的职业机会。
words.en: Lucrative career opportunities refer to job prospects that offer significant financial benefits and potential for growth.

words.tr: adj. 有益健康的；环境宜人的
words.ex: The air in the mountains is salubrious.
words.ex_cn: 山里的空气有益健康。
words.en: A salubrious place is pleasant, healthy, and good for you.

words.tr: phrase. 有益健康的生活方式
words.ex: He leads a salubrious lifestyle by eating vegetables and walking daily.
words.ex_cn: 他通过吃蔬菜和每天散步过着健康的生活方式。
words.en: Conducive or favorable to health or well-being.

words.tr: adj. 值得赞扬的；
words.ex: His commendable effort helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他值得赞扬的努力帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as commendable, you approve of it or are praising it.

words.tr: phrase. 最值得称赞的；极其值得表扬的
words.ex: His most commendable act was helping the old man cross the street.
words.ex_cn: 他最值得称赞的行为是帮助那位老人过马路。
words.en: Deserving praise or approval; highly praiseworthy.

words.tr: adj. 值得赞美的；
words.ex: His laudable effort helped the team win.
words.ex_cn: 他值得赞美的努力帮助团队赢得了比赛。
words.en: Deserving praise and commendation.

words.tr: phrase. 值得称赞的行为；值得赞扬的举动
words.ex: Helping a stranger is a laudable act.
words.ex_cn: 帮助陌生人是一种值得赞扬的行为。
words.en: An action that deserves praise or commendation.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；恶性的；致命的
words.ex: Smoking is a pernicious habit.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟是一种有害的习惯。
words.en: Having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way.

words.tr: phrase. 有害影响；恶劣后果；毒害作用
words.ex: Smoking has pernicious effects on your lungs.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的肺有有害影响。
words.en: Harmful effects that cause great damage or harm, often in a subtle or gradual way.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；造成伤害的
words.ex: Smoking has deleterious effects on your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is deleterious has a harmful effect on something, especially on a person's health.

words.tr: phrase. 有害的；不利的（指对健康、环境或发展等产生负面作用的影响）
words.ex: Smoking has deleterious effects on your lungs.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的肺有有害影响。
words.en: Deleterious effects refer to harmful or damaging consequences that result from a particular action, substance, or condition.

words.tr: adj. 反面假想国的；反面乌托邦的；
words.ex: The movie shows a dystopian future where people have no freedom.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展现了一个没有自由的反面假想国未来。
words.en: A dystopian society is one that is undesirable or frightening, often characterized by totalitarianism, environmental disaster, or other characteristics associated with a cataclysmic decline in society.

words.tr: phrase. 反乌托邦社会；一种描绘为压迫、极权或极端不幸的虚构社会形态
words.ex: The book shows a dystopian society where people have no freedom.
words.ex_cn: 这本书描绘了一个人民没有自由的反乌托邦社会。
words.en: A dystopian society is an imagined state or society in which there is great suffering or injustice, typically one that is totalitarian or post-apocalyptic.

words.tr: adj. 极糟的；极坏的
words.ex: His egregious mistake cost the team the game.
words.ex_cn: 他严重的错误让球队输掉了比赛。
words.en: An egregious error or failure is extremely bad and noticeable.

words.tr: phrase. 极其恶劣的社会；令人震惊的群体
words.ex: The egregious society ignored the poor.
words.ex_cn: 这个恶劣的社会忽视了穷人。
words.en: Characterized by extreme or outrageous behavior; shockingly bad or offensive.

words.tr: adj. 艰巨的；费力的；
words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: Something that is arduous is difficult and tiring, and involves a lot of effort.

words.tr: phrase. 艰巨的任务；困难而费力的工作
words.ex: Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.
words.ex_cn: 爬山是一项艰巨的任务。
words.en: An arduous task is a task that requires a lot of effort and is difficult to accomplish.

words.tr: adj. 繁重的；
words.ex: The onerous workload made her tired every day.
words.ex_cn: 繁重的工作量让她每天都很累。
words.en: If you describe a task as onerous, you dislike having to do it because you find it difficult or unpleasant.

words.tr: phrase. 沉重的负担；繁重的义务
words.ex: He carries an onerous burden every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天背负着沉重的负担。
words.en: An onerous burden refers to a heavy or oppressive load or responsibility that is difficult to bear.

words.tr: adj. 拜占庭风格的；
words.ex: The church has a byzantine dome with gold mosaics.
words.ex_cn: 这座教堂有一个拜占庭风格的穹顶，饰有金色马赛克。
words.en: If you describe a system or process as byzantine, you are criticizing it because it is complicated and difficult to understand.

words.tr: phrase. 复杂得难以理解的状况或系统；极复杂的结构或过程（尤指官僚体系或组织）
words.ex: The rules of the game have byzantine complexity.
words.ex_cn: 这个游戏的规则极其复杂。
words.en: Byzantine complexity refers to something that is extremely complicated and difficult to understand, often resembling the intricate and convoluted systems of the Byzantine Empire.

words.tr: phrase. 无法克服的问题；难以逾越的难题
words.ex: The poverty in that region is an insurmountable problem for many families.
words.ex_cn: 那地区的贫困对许多家庭来说是一个无法克服的问题。
words.en: An insurmountable problem is a problem that is so great that it cannot be dealt with successfully.

words.tr: adj. 可以忽略的；
words.ex: The error is negligible.
words.ex_cn: 这个误差可以忽略。
words.en: If you describe something as negligible, you mean that it is so small or unimportant that it is not worth considering or worrying about.

words.tr: phrase. 可忽略的误差；微不足道的误差
words.ex: The negligible error did not affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 可忽略的误差没有影响结果。
words.en: An error that is so small or unimportant that it can be disregarded.

words.tr: adj. 不重要的；
words.ex: The mistake was trivial and didn't affect the result.
words.ex_cn: 这个错误不重要，没有影响结果。
words.en: If you describe something as trivial, you mean that it is not important or significant, or is not worth serious consideration.

words.tr: phrase. 琐碎的；不重要的细节
words.ex: He ignored the trivial details and focused on the main idea.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了琐碎的细节，专注于主要观点。
words.en: Trivial details refer to small, unimportant pieces of information that are often considered insignificant in the broader context.

words.tr: phrase. 无关紧要的或不相关的
words.ex: His comment was inconsequential or irrelevant to the discussion.
words.ex_cn: 他的评论与讨论无关。
words.en: Having little or no importance, significance, or relevance; trivial.

words.tr: adj. 轻浮的；琐碎的；无意义的
words.ex: His frivolus jokes made everyone uncomfortable.
words.ex_cn: 他轻浮的笑话让每个人都感到不舒服。
words.en: If you describe someone as frivolous, you mean they behave in a silly or light-hearted way, rather than being serious and sensible.

words.tr: phrase. 轻浮的奢侈；不必要的享受；无实际价值的奢华品
words.ex: He spends money on frivolous luxuries like expensive perfumes.
words.ex_cn: 他把钱花在昂贵香水等无谓的奢侈品上。
words.en: Luxuries that are not necessary and are often seen as trivial or wasteful.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.tr: phrase. 至高重要性；头等重要
words.ex: Safety is of paramount importance in the factory.
words.ex_cn: 安全在工厂里至关重要。
words.en: of the greatest importance; supreme.

words.tr: adj. 重要的；关键的；
words.ex: This decision is pivotal for the company's future.
words.ex_cn: 这个决定对公司未来至关重要。
words.en: Of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else.

words.tr: phrase. 关键作用；核心角色
words.ex: She plays a pivotal role in the team.
words.ex_cn: 她在团队中扮演着关键角色。
words.en: A pivotal role is a central or crucial role in a particular situation or activity.

words.tr: adj. 不可缺少的
words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.tr: phrase. 必不可少的要素；不可或缺的组成部分
words.ex: Water is an indispensable element for life.
words.ex_cn: 水是生命不可或缺的元素。
words.en: An indispensable element is something that is absolutely necessary and cannot be done without.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.tr: phrase. 商业上的必然要求；企业必须采取的行动或策略
words.ex: Cutting costs is a business imperative for the company.
words.ex_cn: 降低成本对公司来说是一个商业必需。
words.en: A business imperative is something that is extremely important or essential for the success of a business, often requiring immediate attention or action.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.tr: phrase. 在关键时刻
words.ex: He forgot his lines at the crucial moment.
words.ex_cn: 他在关键时刻忘记了台词。
words.en: At the most important or decisive point in time.

words.tr: n. 不足；缺乏
words.ex: There is a paucity of water in the desert.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠里水很少。
words.en: If you say that there is a paucity of something, you mean that there is not enough of it.

words.tr: phrase. 自然资源的匮乏；自然资源的稀少
words.ex: The country suffers from a paucity of natural resources.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家自然资源匮乏。
words.en: A paucity of natural resources refers to a scarcity or insufficiency of natural materials and substances that are essential for human survival and economic activities.

words.tr: n. 缺乏；
words.ex: There is a dearth of clean water in the village.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄缺乏干净的水。
words.en: A dearth of something is a lack or scarcity of it.

words.tr: phrase. 食物的缺乏；食物短缺
words.ex: There is a dearth of food in the village after the flood.
words.ex_cn: 洪水过后，村里食物严重匮乏。
words.en: A dearth of food refers to a scarcity or lack of food, which can lead to hunger and malnutrition in affected populations.

words.tr: adj. 不足的；欠缺的；微小的；
words.ex: There is scant evidence to support the claim.
words.ex_cn: 支持这一说法的证据不足。
words.en: If you describe something as scant, you mean that there is not enough of it or that it is not as much as it should be.

words.tr: phrase. 稀少的需求；微弱的需求
words.ex: There is scant demand for old radios now.
words.ex_cn: 现在对旧收音机的需求很少。
words.en: A situation where there is very little or insufficient demand for a product or service.

words.tr: adj. 贫乏的；微薄的
words.ex: He had a meager meal after work.
words.ex_cn: 他下班后吃了一顿很少的饭。
words.en: If you describe an amount or quantity of something as meager, you are critical of it because it is very small or not enough.

words.tr: phrase. 微薄的收入；贫乏的收入
words.ex: He has a meager income and struggles to pay rent.
words.ex_cn: 他收入微薄，难以支付房租。
words.en: A very small amount of money earned from work or other sources.

words.tr: n. 过多；过量；过剩；
words.ex: There is a plethora of choices on the menu.
words.ex_cn: 菜单上有太多的选择。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large quantity of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.tr: 短语. 大量的在线资源
words.ex: There is a plethora of online resources for learning English.
words.ex_cn: n. 有大量的在线资源可以用来学习英语。
words.en: A very large amount of something, especially more than you need, want, or can deal with.

words.tr: n. 大量；丰富；慷慨；浪费
words.ex: There is a profusion of flowers in the garden.
words.ex_cn: 花园里有大量花朵。
words.en: If there is a profusion of something or it occurs in profusion, there is a very large quantity or variety of it.

words.tr: 短语. 鱼类大量繁盛，形容鱼群极为丰富、旺盛地生长或聚集
words.ex: The coral reef was teeming with fish in riotous profusion.
words.ex_cn: 珊瑚礁上鱼群大量聚集。
words.en: A large and abundant gathering of fish, often seen in natural habitats like coral reefs or rivers.

words.tr: n. 丰饶的山羊角；聚宝盆；丰饶角
words.ex: The Thanksgiving table had a cornucopia of fruits and vegetables.
words.ex_cn: 感恩节的餐桌上摆满了水果和蔬菜的丰饶山羊角。
words.en: A cornucopia is a symbol of abundance and nourishment, commonly represented as a large horn-shaped container overflowing with produce, flowers, or nuts.

words.tr: phrase. 丰富的选择；大量可供选择的事物
words.ex: The new supermarket offers a cornucopia of choices for organic products.
words.ex_cn: 新超市提供了丰富的有机产品选择。
words.en: A large and varied amount of options or selections.

words.tr:
adj. 无数的；
n. 无数；
words.ex: There are myriad stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数的星星。
words.en: A myriad of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.tr: phrase. 无数的好处；众多的益处
words.ex: The new policy has brought myriad benefits to the community.
words.ex_cn: 新政策给社区带来了无数的好处。
words.en: A countless number of advantages or positive outcomes.

words.tr: phrase. 无数的； myriad 表示极多的数量，a myriad of 意为“大量的，无数的”
words.ex: There are a myriad of stars in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 夜空中有无数的星星。
words.en: A myriad of means a very large number of something, often used to emphasize the vastness or diversity of the items being referred to.

words.tr:
v. 使饮食过度；吃得过量；过分沉溺
n. 过量；过度
words.ex: He surfeited on pizza and felt sick.
words.ex_cn: 他吃太多披萨，感到恶心。
words.en: An excessive amount of something, especially food or drink.

words.tr: phrase. 信息过量；信息过剩
words.ex: The internet has led to a surfeit of information, making it hard to find reliable sources.
words.ex_cn: 互联网导致了信息过剩，使得找到可靠的来源变得困难。
words.en: An excessive amount of information that can be overwhelming or difficult to manage.

words.tr:
v. 触发；引起；发动；
n. 诱因；触发；
words.ex: The loud noise triggered the alarm.
words.ex_cn: 巨大的噪音触发了警报。
words.en: A trigger is a device that activates a mechanism when it is pulled or pressed. It can also refer to something that causes a particular reaction or development.

words.tr: phrase. 引起；导致
words.ex: Poor hygiene can give rise to infections.
words.ex_cn: 不良的卫生习惯可能导致感染。
words.en: To cause something to happen or exist.

words.tr:
v. 加速（坏事的发生）
n. 沉淀物；冷凝物
adj. 轻率的；仓促的
words.ex: The scandal precipitated the politician's resignation.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻加速了这位政治家的辞职。
words.en: To cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly; to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.tr: v. 增强；提高；
words.ex: Exercise can bolster your health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以增强你的健康。
words.en: If you bolster something such as someone's confidence or courage, you increase it. A bolster is also a long, firm pillow.

words.tr: phrase. 贡献；促成；导致；有助于
words.ex: Volunteers contribute to the clean-up of the park.
words.ex_cn: 志愿者们为公园的清洁做出了贡献。
words.en: If you contribute to something, you help to cause it or make it happen.

words.tr: 短语. 大量的；丰富的（用于描述某物数量极多）
words.ex: There is an abundance of apples in the market this season.
words.ex_cn: n. 这个季节市场上有很多苹果。
words.en: A very large quantity of something.

words.tr: adj. 最高的；至上的；最重要的；
words.ex: His safety is paramount.
words.ex_cn: 他的安全是最重要的。
words.en: Something that is paramount or of paramount importance is more important than anything else.

words.tr: adj. 不可缺少的
words.ex: Water is indispensable for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命是必不可少的。
words.en: Absolutely necessary or essential.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.tr: phrase. 进步是不可避免的；发展是必然的
words.ex: Progress is inevitable when you keep trying.
words.ex_cn: 当你不断努力时，进步是不可避免的。
words.en: The idea that forward movement or improvement cannot be stopped.

words.tr: adj. 不注意的；疏忽的；非故意的
words.ex: He made an inadvertent mistake while typing.
words.ex_cn: 他在打字时不小心犯了个错误。
words.en: If something bad is inadvertent, it is done without realizing that it is wrong or that it could have bad consequences.

words.tr: phrase. 促进沟通；使交流更顺畅
words.ex: A good teacher can facilitate communication in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 一位好老师可以在课堂上促进交流。
words.en: To make it easier for people to exchange information or ideas.

words.tr: adj. 有害的；
words.ex: Smoking is detrimental to your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟对你的健康有害。
words.en: Something that is detrimental has a harmful or damaging effect on something else.

words.tr: phrase. 对…有害的；对…造成损害的
words.ex_cn: 过量饮酒可能对健康有害。
words.en: If something is detrimental to something else, it causes harm or damage to it.

words.tr: adj. 密集的；
words.ex: He took an intensive English course last summer.
words.ex_cn: 去年夏天，他参加了一个密集的英语课程。
words.en: Intensive is used to describe something that involves a lot of effort, energy, or attention in a short period of time.

words.tr: phrase. 强化训练；密集培训
words.ex: He does intensive training every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上进行高强度训练。
words.en: Intensive training refers to a concentrated and rigorous program designed to improve skills or knowledge in a specific area within a short period of time.

words.tr: v. 贮藏；收集；得到
words.ex: He garnered food for the winter.
words.ex_cn: 他贮藏了过冬的食物。
words.en: To gather or collect something, especially information or support.

words.tr: phrase. 获得更多的国际关注
words.ex: The new film will garner more international attention.
words.ex_cn: 这部新电影将获得更多国际关注。
words.en: To gain or collect more attention from people around the world.

words.tr: adj. 认知的；
words.ex: Children develop cognitive skills as they grow.
words.ex_cn: 孩子在成长过程中发展认知能力。
words.en: Cognitive means relating to the mental process involved in knowing, learning, and understanding things.

words.tr: phrase. 认知偏差；指人们在处理信息和做出判断时，由于心理倾向而导致的系统性偏离理性思维的错误
words.ex: The study aimed to identify common cognitive biases in decision-making processes.
words.ex_cn: 这项研究旨在识别决策过程中常见的认知偏差。
words.en: A cognitive bias is a systematic pattern of deviation from norm or rationality in judgment, whereby inferences about other people and situations may be drawn in an illogical fashion.

words.tr: adj. 经验主义的；以经验为根据的；
words.ex: The scientist used empirical data to support her theory.
words.ex_cn: 这位科学家使用经验数据来支持她的理论。
words.en: Empirical evidence or study relies on practical experience rather than theories.

words.tr: phrase. 经验证据；基于观察或实验而非理论的证据
words.ex: The scientist found empirical evidence in the data.
words.ex_cn: 科学家在数据中找到了实证证据。
words.en: Empirical evidence is information acquired by observation or experimentation. This data is recorded and used by scientists as a primary source. Scientists record and analyze this data. The process is a central part of the scientific method.

words.tr: adj. 先发制人的；
words.ex: The army took preemptive action to stop the attack.
words.ex_cn: 军队采取了先发制人的行动来阻止攻击。
words.en: A preemptive action is one that is taken in order to prevent something unpleasant from happening.

words.tr: phrase. 抓住先发制人的机会；抢先把握有利时机
words.ex: He took the preemptive opportunities to start his business early.
words.ex_cn: 他抓住了先发制人的机会，早早开始了他的生意。
words.en: To seize the initiative or act before others to gain an advantage.

words.tr: adj. 监管的；
words.ex: The regulatory agency checks food safety.
words.ex_cn: 监管机构检查食品安全。
words.en: Relating to the regulation of something, especially by the government.

words.tr: phrase. 监管机构；负责制定并执行行业法规的政府部门或官方组织
words.ex: The regulatory agency is responsible for monitoring the financial market.
words.ex_cn: 该监管机构负责监控金融市场。
words.en: A regulatory agency is a public authority or government agency responsible for exercising autonomous authority over some area of human activity in a regulatory or supervisory capacity.

words.tr: adj. 前所未有的；
words.ex: The storm caused unprecedented damage.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴造成了前所未有的破坏。
words.en: If something is unprecedented, it has never happened before.

words.tr: phrase. 前所未有的成功
words.ex: The company achieved unprecedented success with its latest product launch.
words.ex_cn: 该公司凭借其最新产品发布取得了空前的成功。
words.en: Unprecedented success refers to a level of achievement that has never been seen or experienced before.

words.tr: phrase. 更不用说；何况
words.ex: He can't even walk, let alone run.
words.ex_cn: 他连走都走不了，更别说跑了。
words.en: Used to emphasize the improbability of a contrasting example.

words.tr: v. 证明；展示；
words.ex: The experiment demonstrates that water boils at 100°C.
words.ex_cn: 这个实验证明水在100摄氏度时沸腾。
words.en: To demonstrate means to show something clearly by giving proof or evidence.

words.tr: v. 容纳；适应；为...提供住宿；
words.ex: The hotel can accommodate 200 guests.
words.ex_cn: 这家酒店能容纳200位客人。
words.en: If a building or space can accommodate someone or something, it has enough room for them.

words.tr: n. 过多；过量；过剩；
words.ex: There is a plethora of choices on the menu.
words.ex_cn: 菜单上有太多的选择。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large quantity of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.tr: 短语. 大量的；过剩的（用于描述某物数量过多）
words.ex: There is a plethora of information available on the internet.
words.ex_cn: 互联网上有大量的信息可供查阅。
words.en: A plethora of something is a very large amount of it, especially an amount that is greater than you need, want, or can cope with.

words.tr: n. 相互作用；相互影响；互动交流；
words.ex: The interaction between the two chemicals causes a reaction.
words.ex_cn: 这两种化学物质之间的相互作用引起反应。
words.en: An interaction is a situation where two or more people or things communicate with or react to each other.

words.tr: v. 促进；使便利；使容易；
words.ex: The teacher facilitates learning by asking questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师通过提问来促进学习。
words.en: To make an action or process easier or more likely to happen.

words.tr: phrase. 与…一致；符合；与…相符
words.ex: Her decision is in line with the company's policy.
words.ex_cn: 她的决定与公司的政策一致。
words.en: To be in agreement or conformity with something.

words.tr: n. 万应药；灵丹妙药；
words.ex: He thinks this new pill is a panacea for all diseases.
words.ex_cn: 他认为这种新药是治百病的万应药。
words.en: A panacea is a remedy for all diseases or ills.

words.tr: v. 主张；竞争；
words.ex: He contends that education is the key to success.
words.ex_cn: 他主张教育是成功的关键。
words.en: If you contend with someone or contend with something, you have to deal with a difficult situation or problem. If you contend that something is true, you state or argue that it is true.

words.tr: phrase. 应对，处理（困难或挑战）；与…竞争
words.ex: He has to contend with heavy traffic every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都要应对严重的交通拥堵。
words.en: To contend with something means to have to deal with a difficult or unpleasant situation.

words.tr: v. 处理；
words.ex: He will tackle the problem tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会处理这个问题。
words.en: If you tackle a problem or task, you deal with it in a determined way. In sports such as football and rugby, a tackle is an act of trying to take the ball from a player on the other team.

words.tr: phrase. 应对腐败；处理贪污问题
words.ex: The government has introduced new laws to tackle corruption effectively.
words.ex_cn: 政府已经引入了新的法律来有效处理腐败。
words.en: To tackle corruption means to take action to deal with or solve the problem of corruption, which involves dishonest or fraudulent conduct by those in power.

words.tr: v. 实现；
words.ex: He worked hard to fulfill his dream.
words.ex_cn: 他努力工作以实现自己的梦想。
words.en: To fulfill a task, role, or function means to do or perform it as required or expected.

words.tr: phrase. 履行义务；完成责任
words.ex: It is important to fulfill obligations in a timely manner.
words.ex_cn: 及时履行义务是很重要的。
words.en: To fulfill an obligation means to do something that you are legally or morally required to do.

words.tr: n. 改革；改造；
words.ex: The government announced a major reform in education.
words.ex_cn: 政府宣布了教育方面的重大改革。
words.en: If someone reforms a system, they change or improve it.

words.tr: n. 创新；
words.ex: The company values innovation in its products.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司重视产品的创新。
words.en: Innovation is the introduction of new ideas, methods, or things.

words.tr: adj. 不可阻挡的；
words.ex: The inexorable flow of time cannot be stopped.
words.ex_cn: 时间不可阻挡地流逝。
words.en: If you describe something as inexorable, you mean that it is impossible to stop or prevent from happening.

words.tr: phrase. 不可阻挡的全球化；无法遏止的全球一体化进程
words.ex: The inexorable globalization of markets has changed the way businesses operate.
words.ex_cn: 不可阻挡的市场全球化已经改变了企业的运营方式。
words.en: The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale, which is unstoppable.

words.tr: n. 规定；契约；制定
words.ex: The contract has a stipulation about payment dates.
words.ex_cn: 合同中有关于付款日期的规定。
words.en: A stipulation is a condition or requirement that is specified as part of an agreement or contract.

words.tr: phrase. 合同条款；契约中的规定
words.ex: The contractual stipulation requires both parties to fulfill their obligations.
words.ex_cn: 合同规定要求双方履行各自的义务。
words.en: A contractual stipulation is a specific condition or requirement that is included in a contract, which must be adhered to by the parties involved.

words.tr: phrase. 出发；动身；使爆炸；引起
words.ex: He set off early to avoid traffic.
words.ex_cn: 他早早出发以避开交通拥堵。
words.en: To begin a journey or to cause something to start or happen.

words.tr: phrase. 不停地唠叨某事；反复抱怨
words.ex: She kept harping on about her new job.
words.ex_cn: 她不停地谈论她的新工作。
words.en: To talk or complain about something repeatedly and in a way that is annoying.

words.tr: phrase. 逐步增加；快速提升；加大（生产、速度、力度等）
words.ex: The company plans to ramp up production next quarter.
words.ex_cn: 公司计划在下个季度逐步增加生产。
words.en: To increase or cause to increase in amount, intensity, or extent.

words.tr: n. 支持者；拥护者；辩护者
words.ex: He is a proponent of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 他是清洁能源的支持者。
words.en: A proponent of an idea or course of action is someone who supports it and tries to persuade other people to support it.

words.tr: n. 对手；
words.ex: He defeated his opponent in the chess game.
words.ex_cn: 他在国际象棋比赛中击败了对手。
words.en: An opponent is someone who is competing against you in a contest, game, or argument, or someone who is opposed to an idea or plan.

words.tr: v. 使缠绕，使交织
words.ex: The vines interwind around the fence.
words.ex_cn: 藤蔓缠绕在围栏上。
words.en: To twist or weave together; to intertwine.

words.tr: vi. 发出火星，发出闪光（spark的过去式与过去分词形式）
words.ex: The match sparked when it hit the ground.
words.ex_cn: 火柴撞到地上时迸出了火星。
words.en: To cause something to start or develop, especially suddenly.

words.tr:
v. 把…归因于；由…引起；
n. 品质；属性；特征；属性；
words.ex: He attributes his success to hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的成功归因于努力工作。
words.en: If you attribute something to an event or situation, you think that it was caused by that event or situation.

words.tr: adj. 足够的；
words.ex: There is ample food for everyone.
words.ex_cn: 每个人都有足够的食物。
words.en: If there is an ample amount of something, there is enough of it and usually some extra.

words.tr: phrase. 充足的供应；丰富的供给
words.ex: The region has an ample supply of fresh water.
words.ex_cn: 该地区有充足的淡水供应。
words.en: A sufficient or more than adequate amount of something that is available for use.

words.tr: n. 最佳化
words.ex: He is working on optimization of the system.
words.ex_cn: 他正在改进系统的优化。
words.en: Optimization refers to the process of making something as good or as effective as possible.

words.tr: adj. 非凡的；不平常的；
words.ex: She has an extraordinary talent for music.
words.ex_cn: 她具有非凡的音乐天赋。
words.en: Something that is extraordinary is very unusual or remarkable.

words.tr: n. 政治家，政客
words.ex: The politico spoke at the town meeting.
words.ex_cn: 这位政界人士在 town 会议上发表了讲话。
words.en: A politico is a politician or someone who is involved in politics, often used to suggest that the person is more interested in power than in principles.

words.tr: n. 动机；诱因；
words.ex: The bonus is an incentive to work harder.
words.ex_cn: 奖金是努力工作的动机。
words.en: Something that encourages a person to do something or to work harder.

words.tr: n. 不足额；
words.ex: The country has a budget deficit this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年这个国家的预算不足额。
words.en: A deficit is the amount by which something, especially a sum of money, is too small.

words.tr: v. 显现；
words.ex: His sadness manifested in his quiet eyes.
words.ex_cn: 他的悲伤表现在他安静的眼神中。
words.en: To manifest something means to show it clearly and visibly.

words.tr: n. 例证；
words.ex: The story includes an illustration of kindness.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事包含了一个善良的例证。
words.en: An illustration is a picture or diagram that helps make something clear or attractive.

words.tr: v. 促进；推动；宣传；推销；
words.ex: Exercise can promote good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼可以促进健康。
words.en: To promote means to help something to happen, develop, or increase, or to raise someone to a higher position or rank.

words.tr: phrase. 即时因果报应；立刻得到报应
words.ex: He lied to his boss and got fired the same day—instant karma.
words.ex_cn: 他对老板撒谎，结果当天就被解雇了——这就是即时因果报应。
words.en: Instant karma refers to the immediate consequences of one's actions, often seen as a form of cosmic justice.

words.tr: n. （进退两难的）窘境
words.ex: He faced a dilemma: stay home or go to work.
words.ex_cn: 他面临一个困境：是待在家里还是去上班。
words.en: A situation in which a difficult choice has to be made between two or more alternatives, especially equally undesirable ones.

words.tr:
adj. 精心制作的；详尽的；
v. 精心制作；详尽阐述；
words.ex: She wore an elaborate dress to the party.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件精心制作的裙子去参加派对。
words.en: To elaborate means to add more details to something that has already been said or written, making it more complex or detailed. As an adjective, it describes something that is very complex and detailed.

words.tr: n. 讽刺作品；
words.ex: The movie is a satire about politicians.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部关于政治家的讽刺作品。
words.en: A way of criticizing people or ideas in a humorous way, especially in order to make a political point, or a piece of writing that uses this style.

words.tr:
adj. 交替的；轮流的；间隔的；
v. （使）交替；（使）轮流；
words.ex: We take alternate days off work.
words.ex_cn: 我们隔天休息一次。
words.en: If something alternates between two things, it repeatedly changes from one to the other and back again.

words.tr: adj. 原始的；
words.ex: The primal forest has never been touched by humans.
words.ex_cn: 这片原始森林从未被人类触碰过。
words.en: Primal means relating to an early stage in the development of something, or being the most important or basic part of something.

words.tr: n. 大量；众多；群众；
words.ex: A multitude of people attended the festival.
words.ex_cn: 大量的人参加了这个节日。
words.en: A multitude of things or people is a very large number of them.

words.tr: v. 强迫；迫使
words.ex: They tried to coerce him into signing the paper.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图强迫他签署那份文件。
words.en: If you coerce someone into doing something, you make them do it, even though they do not want to.

words.tr: v. 贡献；促成；捐献；投稿；
words.ex: He contributes money to the charity.
words.ex_cn: 他向慈善机构捐款。
words.en: If you contribute to something, you help to cause it or make it happen.

words.tr: n. 危险
words.ex: He put his job in jeopardy by being late every day.
words.ex_cn: 他因为每天迟到而危及了自己的工作。
words.en: Jeopardy is a situation of exposure to danger or harm.

words.tr: v. 侵犯；侵略；
words.ex: The army tried to invade the neighboring country.
words.ex_cn: 军队试图侵犯邻国。
words.en: To enter a country, town, or region by force in order to take control of it.

words.tr: n. 繁荣；兴旺；
words.ex: The country enjoys prosperity after years of peace.
words.ex_cn: 这个国家在多年的和平后迎来了繁荣。
words.en: Prosperity is a condition in which a person, community, or country is thriving and successful, especially in financial terms.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；
words.ex: Water is vital for life.
words.ex_cn: 水对生命至关重要。
words.en: If you say that something is vital, you mean that it is necessary or very important.

words.tr: v. 下陷；消退；平息
words.ex: The ground began to subside after the heavy rain.
words.ex_cn: 大雨之后，地面开始下陷。
words.en: If a feeling or noise subsides, it becomes less strong or loud.

words.tr: adj. 似乎合理的；看似真实的；似乎可信的；看似真实的；
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible.
words.ex_cn: 他的借口听起来似乎合理。
words.en: An explanation or statement that is plausible seems likely to be true or valid.

words.tr: v. 推测；思索；
words.ex: He speculates that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you speculate about something, you make guesses about its nature or identity, or about what might happen.

words.tr: v. 投入；
words.ex: He devotes his time to helping children.
words.ex_cn: 他投入时间帮助孩子们。
words.en: If you devote yourself, your time, or your energy to something, you spend all or most of your time or energy on it.

words.tr: v. 并置；并列
words.ex: He juxtaposes old photos with new ones.
words.ex_cn: 他把老照片和新照片放在一起。
words.en: To place or deal with close together for contrasting effect.

words.tr: v. 排水；
words.ex: The rainwater drains into the street.
words.ex_cn: 雨水排入街道。
words.en: If you drain something, you remove the liquid from it, usually by pouring it away or by allowing it to flow away. If something drains, the liquid flows away from it.

words.tr: adj. 徒劳的；
words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.tr: v. 传授；给予；告知
words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.tr: v. 揭露；泄露；显露；
words.ex: The letter revealed his secret.
words.ex_cn: 这封信揭露了他的秘密。
words.en: To reveal something means to make known something that was previously secret or unknown.

words.tr: adj. 不透明的；难懂的；晦涩的
words.ex: The glass is opaque, so I cannot see through it.
words.ex_cn: 这扇玻璃是不透明的，所以我看不到它后面的东西。
words.en: If an object or substance is opaque, you cannot see through it.

words.tr: n. 摘要；纲要
words.ex: He read a compendium of math rules.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本数学规则的汇编。
words.en: A compendium is a short but complete collection of information, usually in a book.

words.tr: n. 更新；复兴；
words.ex: The renewal of the contract took one week.
words.ex_cn: 合同的更新花了一周时间。
words.en: The act of making something valid for a further period of time after it has expired or been canceled.

words.tr: adj. 深远的；深刻的；
words.ex: His words had a profound effect on her life.
words.ex_cn: 他的话对她的生活产生了深远的影响。
words.en: If you describe something as profound, you mean that it is very great or intense.

words.tr: adj. 大量的；重大的；实质性的；
words.ex: He made a substantial profit from the sale.
words.ex_cn: 他从这次销售中获得了大量的利润。
words.en: Something that is substantial is large in size, amount, or importance.

words.tr: adj. 巨大的；极大的；
words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.tr: n. 基础设施
words.ex: The city needs better infrastructure for roads and water.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市需要更好的道路和供水设施。
words.en: The basic physical and organizational structures and facilities (e.g., buildings, roads, power supplies) needed for the operation of a society or enterprise.

words.tr: adj. 真正的；真诚的；
words.ex: This is a genuine diamond.
words.ex_cn: 这是一颗真正的钻石。
words.en: If something is genuine, it is real and exactly what it appears to be.

words.tr: n. 剥夺；匮乏；丧失；
words.ex: The prisoners suffered from sleep deprivation.
words.ex_cn: 囚犯们因睡眠剥夺而受苦。
words.en: Deprivation is the lack or denial of something considered to be a necessity.

words.tr: adj. 有（身体或智力）缺陷的；出毛病的；受损的； v. “impair”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The impaired child needs extra help in school.
words.ex_cn: 这个有智力缺陷的孩子需要在学校得到额外的帮助。
words.en: If someone's physical or mental abilities are impaired, they are damaged or weakened, often permanently.

words.tr: v. 居住；（性质）存在；
words.ex: They reside in a small house near the park.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在公园附近的一所小房子里。
words.en: If someone resides somewhere, they live there or are staying there.

words.tr: v. 停息；停止
words.ex: The rain ceased after an hour.
words.ex_cn: 一小时后，雨停了。
words.en: If something ceases, it stops happening or existing.

words.tr: v. 引出；
words.ex: The teacher asked a simple question to elicit answers from students.
words.ex_cn: 老师问了一个简单的问题来引出学生的回答。
words.en: To elicit a response or a reaction means to cause it to happen by something that you say or do.

words.tr: v. 接着发生；因而产生
words.ex: The storm ended, and peace ensued.
words.ex_cn: 风暴结束后，和平随之而来。
words.en: If something ensues, it happens immediately after another event, usually as a result of it.

words.tr: n. 隐喻；比喻；
words.ex: Calling time a thief is a metaphor.
words.ex_cn: 把时间称为小偷是一种隐喻。
words.en: A metaphor is a figure of speech in which a word or phrase is applied to an object or action to which it is not literally applicable.

words.tr: n. 壮举；功绩；
words.ex: Climbing the mountain without oxygen was a great feat.
words.ex_cn: 在不吸氧的情况下爬山是一项伟大的壮举。
words.en: A feat is an act or achievement that shows great courage, skill, or strength.

words.tr: n. 义务；
words.ex: He felt an obligation to help his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他感到有义务帮助他的朋友。
words.en: An obligation is something that you must do because you have promised, because of a law, etc.

words.tr: adj. 传染性的；有感染力的；
words.ex: The virus is infectious and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒具有传染性，传播迅速。
words.en: An infectious disease can be passed from one person to another, especially through the air they breathe.
